methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prespecified cohort analysis of 83 NSCLC patients from the phase Ib portion of a first-in-human open-label multicenter phase Ia/Ib trial (NCT05194982) at five Chinese centers. Primary endpoint is safety; efficacy endpoints (ORR, DCR, DOR) are secondary and PFS/OS are exploratory. Strengths include prespecified cohort stratification by GA type, RECIST v1.1 assessment, and appropriate descriptive statistics with Clopper-Pearson CIs and Kaplan-Meier time-to-event analyses. Key weaknesses: single-arm uncontrolled design, small per-cohort sample sizes (14-26 patients), relatively short median follow-up (7.3 months for OS, 8.2 months for PFS), reliance on local investigator assessment and local genomic testing (no central BICR or genomic confirmation), and no multiplicity adjustment across subgroup comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-arm phase Ib cohort analysis (Oxford level 4). Clinical relevance is meaningful because it addresses a therapeutically underserved NSCLC population with non-classical EGFR, HER2, KRAS, BRAF, MET mutations and ALK/ROS1/RET/NTRK fusions after failure of standard therapy. The 69.2% ORR and 10.5-month median PFS in the EGFR exon20ins/nonclassical cohort and 52.9% ORR in HER2-mutant disease are clinically promising signals for a bispecific EGFR-HER3 ADC, but the authors explicitly note that most patients had not received recently approved standards (amivantamab, sunvozertinib, T-DXd, zongertinib), so sequencing remains uncertain.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05194982 and CTR20212923, provides a trial profile (Fig 1), baseline characteristics (Table 1), TRAEs by grade (Table 2), and efficacy outcomes by subgroup (Table 3). However, a full CONSORT-style flow with exact numbers per cohort is deferred to the Data Supplement, and several important tables (S2-S8 with GA subtype details, detailed TRAE categorizations) are also in the supplement. No explicit data or code availability statement is visible in the main text. Reporting of the prespecified subgroup analyses would benefit from explicit protocol-anchored definitions.

novelty_literature.justification: Iza-bren (BL-B01D1) is described as a first-in-class bispecific ADC simultaneously targeting EGFR and HER3 with a topoisomerase I payload (DAR 8). Extending a bispecific ADC to a genomically heterogeneous NSCLC population beyond classical EGFR is a meaningful novel application, contrasting with monospecific ADCs (T-DXd, Dato-DXd, patritumab deruxtecan). Novelty is tempered by the active ADC field in NSCLC and the ethnic-specific single-country cohort, but the bispecific target combination and broad GA coverage are genuinely new.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is concise and clearly organized with sections covering design, safety, overall efficacy, and prespecified GA subgroups. The discussion honestly positions iza-bren against rapidly evolving competitors (amivantamab, sunvozertinib, T-DXd, zongertinib) and appropriately lists limitations including small cohorts, single-country enrollment, short follow-up, local assessment, and limited brain metastases experience. Tables 1-3 and Figs 1-2 are well constructed. A few sections of the Results text contain orphan caption fragments that should be cleaned up.

key_strengths: First clinical evaluation of a first-in-class bispecific EGFR-HER3 ADC (iza-bren) in a diverse NSCLC population with actionable GAs beyond classical EGFR
Encouraging response signals including 69.2% ORR and 10.5-month mPFS in EGFR exon20ins/nonclassical cohort and 52.9% ORR in HER2-mutant disease
Manageable safety profile with predominantly manageable hematologic TRAEs and low (1.4%) grade 2 ILD rate compared with T-DXd benchmarks
Prespecified GA-stratified cohort analysis with Clopper-Pearson CIs and Brookmeyer-Crowley time-to-event estimates
key_concerns: Single-arm uncontrolled phase Ib design with no randomized comparator and potential selection bias
Small per-subgroup cohorts (EGFR exon20ins/nonclassical n=13, HER2 n=19, KRAS/BRAF/MET n=26, fusions n=24) limiting inference
Relatively short median follow-up (OS 7.3 months) with immature survival data
Single-country (China) enrollment and local genomic and radiologic assessment limit generalizability
Most patients had not received recently approved targeted therapies (amivantamab, T-DXd, zongertinib), leaving treatment sequencing unresolved
No explicit data/code availability statement in the main text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-designed phase Ib cohort report of a novel bispecific ADC with encouraging activity in a therapeutically underserved NSCLC population; appropriate for a top-tier oncology journal with minor revisions to clarify cohort composition and data sharing, although validation in controlled multinational studies is needed.
